items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: I remember with Woody’s band we played in Madison, Wisconsin

ctx.x: Did you have a moment in a studio date where you started to see the technology enter the picture, either with replacing people or different ways of, you know, overdubbing and all that. Do you recall when that started to creep into the scene?

Yeah. When I started there was not so much tracking you know, multiple tracking, so you had to play it right the first time you know, or every time. And then when the multiple tracking came in and punching in tracks like — guys wouldn’t have the pressure to play correctly the first time. You know what I mean? ‘Cause they knew that they could re-do a mistake. That had an influence I believe. And also when the mix ended up being with the engineer — like I remember with Woody’s band we played in Madison, Wisconsin…
That’s a very interesting take on the effect on the musicians being less demanding about their own performance.
